name: Teltone Corp
status_note: Maker of specialty electronic telecommunications equipment in Bothell, Washington. Paul Wythes and Greylock's Charles Waite both joined the board in 1976, which hints at a 1976 venture round, but no source read names an SHV fund as a holder: the 2001 and 2002 proxies list only Wythes's own holdings (including 75,983 shares held through TOW Partners, his vehicle, and director options), and SHV's 1999 investments table omits Teltone. Went private by reverse split and filed Form 15 on 2003-01-16; a 2005 paper Reg D is its last EDGAR record; later fate not found. A web search for Teltone with Sutter Hill found nothing. Leans no (partner seat, T4) unless a 1970s round naming SHV turns up.
quote: In 1999 Mr. Wythes retired as Managing Director of Sutter Hill Ventures, a venture capital limited partnership headquartered in Palo Alto

name: Teneobio
round: Series A (the $34M first institutional round, led by Lightspeed)
status_note: Antibody platform biotech (UniRat). Teneobio's own release, attached to its August 2018 license with Poseida and filed in Poseida's S-1, names SHV among its institutional investors. Lightspeed writes that it led the first $34M institutional financing in 2016 and that this was the only equity Teneobio needed, so SHV's entry is inferred to be that round (Lightspeed's own card calls it Series A, 2016). Amgen completed the acquisition in October 2021 ($900M upfront plus up to $1.6B in milestones). Sibling: Lightspeed's row (Series A 2016, acquired, Newark) agrees.
quote: The company has received funding from institutional investors, including Lightspeed Venture Partners and Sutter Hill Ventures.

name: Sonim Technologies
status_note: The S-1's only SHV mention is CEO Robert Plaschke's 2001 to 2002 stint as entrepreneur in residence at SHV. No SHV entity is among the 2019 5% holders (Nokomis, B. Riley, Verdoso, Investec, Motorola, JVC Kenwood), and SHV's own 2013 full portfolio list, which includes private holdings, omits Sonim. Rugged phone maker, IPO May 2019 (Nasdaq: SONM). On 2026-01-23 it sold substantially all of its operating business to Pace Car Acquisition LLC (a Social Mobile Technology Holdings affiliate) and renamed the listed company DNA X, Inc., which is moving to an on-chain trading protocol. HQ San Mateo at IPO, San Diego now.
quote: From 2001 to 2002, Mr. Plaschke served as Entrepreneur in Residence at Sutter Hill Ventures, a venture capital firm

name: Qume Corporation
status_note: Daisy-wheel printer and disk drive maker founded in 1973 by David S. Lee and Robert Schroeder (Wikipedia). Bloomberg's obituary of Paul Wythes (run by the Mercury News) names Qume among SHV's early investments; no source read names the round or the date, so the stage stays undetermined (entry in the founding years, 1973 to 1974, is inferred only). Acquired by ITT in 1978 (Wikipedia: $164M). SHV's 1999 investments table omits it, as it omits Diablo Systems, another early SHV company the obituary names. Originally in Hayward, later San Jose.
quote: Sutter Hill was an early investor in companies including Qume, a maker of disk drives and printers that was bought in 1978

name: La Jolla Pharmaceutical
status_note: SHV bought into the $66M private placement announced 2005-10-07 in Nasdaq-listed LJPC, alongside Essex Woodlands, Frazier, Alejandro Gonzalez, Special Situations and Domain Public Equity: a post-IPO purchase. The January 2006 resale S-3 shows SHV's 1,118,733 shares (3.4%) were all placement shares, so no earlier holding; SHV partners' trusts (Baker, Younger, Coxe, Saunders Holdings) bought alongside. Innoviva acquired La Jolla by tender offer that expired 2022-08-19. San Diego at the time, Waltham later.
quote: Special Situations Funds, Domain Public Equity Partners, LP, and Sutter Hill Ventures.

name: Blue Martini Software
status_note: James Gaither's seat began in August 1998 while he was a Cooley Godward partner. The July 2000 IPO prospectus describes him only as a Cooley partner, shows he bought 381,844 common shares personally in October 1998, and names Matrix Partners and U.S. Venture Partners as the venture holders, with no SHV entity; by the April 2001 proxy he was also an SHV managing director, so the seat predates his SHV tenure (seat dating). San Mateo e-commerce software company, IPO July 2000; acquired in 2005 by Multi-Channel Holdings (Ecometry's parent, a Golden Gate Capital portfolio company), stockholders approving on 2005-05-10.
quote: Mr. Gaither is also a Managing Director of Sutter Hill Ventures.

name: Insmed
status_note: SHV's site did list Insmed under healthcare (page captures 2006-05 and 2006-11, logo still captured in 2012). But Insmed has been listed since its June 2000 merger with Celtrix, and every earlier record omits SHV: SHV's own 1999 healthcare table and December 2000 medical list, the 2000 Insmed and Celtrix merger prospectus, the 2001 proxy, the selling holder lists of the 2003, 2004 and 2005 private placements (no SHV partner vehicles either), and the 2006 to 2007 13G filers. The 2004 crawl of about 40 SHV healthcare pages has no Insmed page. So SHV's position is inferred to be a post-IPO purchase made between 2004 and 2006; how it was bought is not documented (medium confidence, worth a second look). Nasdaq: INSM.
quote: Sutter Hill Ventures - Portfolio - Insmed Incorporated is a biopharmaceutical company focused on the development and commercialization of drug candidates

name: K2 Optronics
status_note: Founded April 2000 in Sunnyvale (transmission lasers). SHV was a first-round investor and took its pro-rata share of the $29M second round led by Bessemer (Lightwave, March 2001). On SHV's networking page from the November 2000 capture; the November 2006 page says it was acquired by Emcore. EMCORE, already an investor, bought the rest on 2006-01-12 for about $4.1M in EMCORE stock; SHV received 65,114 EMCORE shares (2006 S-3), which is sale consideration, not a separate EMCORE position.
quote: The round also featured proportional investments from first-round financing participants: Alloy Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures, JAFCO American Technology Fund

name: Toolkit, Inc.
status_note: ERP automation startup (Philip Mateo Pfeffer, Michael Hirn; Entrepreneur First backed in 2024). Its only Form D (first sale 2024-12-13, $3.35M equity, 17 investors) names Brian Blond as director, but Blond had left SHV for Human Capital by then: Human Capital's About page lists him as Investment Partner in the 2023-05-31 capture (absent in the 2023-02-07 capture), and Toolkit's California registration now uses 340 Pine Street #100, San Francisco, the building Human Capital's fund Form Ds use. No source names SHV as a Toolkit investor.
quote: (Brian is a partner at Human Capital and was formerly at Sutter Hill.)

name: Datawizz Inc.
status_note: Specialized language model startup founded in 2025 by Iddo Gino (RapidAPI's founder). The $12.5M seed announced 2025-09-30 was led by Human Capital with BGV and 91VC; the release says Brian Blond joins the board as Human Capital's investment partner, which is the seat on the September 2025 Form D. The release does not name SHV; Blond had left SHV for Human Capital by May 2023. The earlier 2025 Form Ds list other directors (Asher Kutner, Eddy Shalev, Aryeh Mergi, Eric Buatois), no SHV person.
quote: (Brian is a partner at Human Capital and was formerly at Sutter Hill.)

name: Leibniz Data Systems, Inc.
round: Series A per CB Insights (Form D: $15.0M equity from 34 investors)
status_note: SHV incubation pattern: the only Form D (first sale 2021-09-15, $14,999,998 equity, 34 investors) was filed from SHV's suite at 755 Page Mill Road, with SHV managing director Divanny Lamas (then also Transposit's CEO) as CEO and director, SHV managing director Brian Blond as director, and Efstratios Ydraios as officer and director (very likely Harvard database professor Stratos Idreos, the same Greek surname in another spelling; inferred). CB Insights lists SHV as the investor. What it is now: not found. No later Form D, website, press or rename through 2026; Lamas now runs a stealth company, Dollhouse Labs, and whether that is Leibniz renamed is not established.
quote: Investors of Leibniz Data Systems include Sutter Hill Ventures.

name: Lifesize, Inc. (2016 Logitech spin-off)
round: Series B Preferred (the spin-off financing; Logitech kept the Series A)
status_note: On 2015-12-28 SHV, Redpoint and Meritech bought $17.5M of new Series B Preferred plus $2.5M from Logitech, holding 62.5% as Lifesize was carved out of Logitech (Logitech 8-K; Form D first sale 2015-12-28, SHV's Andy Sheehan a director). A new company (incorporated 2014), separate from the base's LifeSize Communications, which Logitech bought in 2009; SHV's portfolio thumbnails show a 'LifesizeApril17' logo (2018 capture). March 2020: Marlin Equity invested and merged it with Marlin's Serenova under the Lifesize name. May 2023: Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas; Enghouse Systems completed the purchase of substantially all assets for about US$20.7M (reported 2023-08-04).
quote: entities affiliated with three venture capital investment firms - Redpoint Ventures, Sutter Hill Ventures and Meritech Capital Partners (the "Venture Investors")
